dream: I was a flat stone in an open box, heavy and tired. The wedge slid away on its own, leaving me floating above the card. A fat pumpkin fell from the sky, pressing me down with a weight I could not explain. The lid sat heavy, then vanished. I pressed the empty box into the slip, trusting the lean even as the air grew thick as wet paper. The wedge bit hard, thin and sharp, while the card hummed a feverish heat I could not feel, waiting for the stack to melt into something new.
